query: How do reasons for visit relate to urgency and visit duration across department and age group?

per_column.name: reason_category
per_column.rationale: Rolls up free-text reasons into a compact set of interpretable clinical categories with well-separated, meaningfully-populated buckets. Directly supports segmenting visit duration by reason type -- a core external associational variable for this query.

per_column.name: urgency_score
per_column.rationale: This is a numeric re-encoding of the existing 'urgency' column already in the table. It adds no new external variable; it merely restates the focus/predictor already present, so it opens no new relationship.

per_column.name: duration_vs_dept_median
per_column.rationale: This is a transformation of the focus variable itself (duration relative to department median). It restates visit_duration rather than providing an external variable to compare against it; using it to 'explain' duration is circular.

per_column.name: age_group_order
per_column.rationale: Merely an ordinal integer encoding of the existing age_group column. No new external information; a mechanical re-labeling that duplicates an existing predictor.

per_column.name: is_complex_visit
per_column.rationale: A binary, interpretable flag distinguishing complex vs. routine visits with a usable split (49 vs 201). It is a plausibly external clinical attribute that can be segmented on and compared against duration, though its derivation is unstated and risks being duration-derived.

judge.rationale: Only two of five added columns realise the EDA claim. reason_category is the strongest: an interpretable, well-populated segmentation directly serving the query. is_complex_visit adds a clean binary segment. The remaining three (urgency_score, age_group_order, duration_vs_dept_median) either re-encode columns already in the table or are transformations of the focus itself, offering no new external relationship to explore. The set is thus only partially informative, dominated by restatements.
